findings.evidence: Lines 96–114 use the invertibility assumption only to form `QuadraticMap.associated Q` and invoke `associated_isOrtho`; `QuadraticMap.polarBilin` is defined without this assumption in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean:320, with `isOrtho_polarBilin` at line 1049.
findings.fix: State both declarations using `LinearMap.BilinForm.orthogonal Q.polarBilin W` and prove the cross term vanishes via `QuadraticMap.isOrtho_polarBilin`; then weaken the ambient classes as far as that construction permits.
findings.issue: `IsometryEquiv.prodRestrictOrthogonal` and its application lemma unnecessarily require `[Invertible (2 : R)]`; the isometry only needs complementary submodules orthogonal for `Q.polarBilin`.

summary: The orthogonal-decomposition API carries an unnecessary invertibility-of-two restriction by defining orthogonality through the associated form instead of the universally available polar form.
